Build the jsonl-lint tool as a new npm workspace and open one PR for https://github.com/suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test/issues/102. The repo currently has no packages/ directory; the root package.json already declares workspaces packages/* and runs every workspace's tests with npm test. CI (.github/workflows/test.yml) runs npm ci then npm test on Node 22.

Steps:
1. Create packages/jsonl-lint/package.json: "name": "jsonl-lint", "type": "module", "scripts": { "test": "node --test" }, a "bin": { "jsonl-lint": "bin/jsonl-lint.js" } entry, "private": true, and NO "dependencies" field (no runtime dependencies at all). Plain ES modules, no build step, Node 22+.
2. Create packages/jsonl-lint/src/index.js exporting a named function lint(text) that returns an array of { line, error } objects (exactly those two keys): split text on \n (strip a trailing \r per line), number lines 1-based, skip lines that are empty or whitespace-only, run JSON.parse on every other line, and for each that throws push { line: <1-based number>, error: <the error message, non-empty string> }. The last line counts even when the text does not end with a newline (a torn/unterminated last row like {"c": must be reported). Valid text returns [].
3. Create packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js (shebang #!/usr/bin/env node, chmod +x): takes one file path argument. With no argument, print a usage message to stderr and exit 2. If the file cannot be read (missing), print a message to stderr and exit 2. Otherwise read it as UTF-8, call lint, and for each result print to stdout exactly `<file>:<line>: <error>` where <file> is the path argument as given; exit 1 if there was at least one result, 0 if none (printing nothing on stdout for a clean file).
4. Add node:test tests under packages/jsonl-lint/test/ (e.g. test/lint.test.js, which node --test picks up by default) covering: a clean file (no errors, CLI exit 0), a bad middle row (reported with the correct 1-based line), a torn last row with no trailing newline (reported), blank lines (skipped, and they do not shift line numbers of later rows), and the CLI exit codes 0, 1 and 2 (missing file and no argument; spawn the bin with child_process.spawnSync(process.execPath, [binPath, ...]) and use temp files from fs.mkdtempSync(os.tmpdir())).
5. Create packages/jsonl-lint/README.md describing usage of the CLI and lint(text), output format and exit codes. Update the root README.md: replace the "No tools yet" bullet under "What is here" with a bullet listing packages/jsonl-lint (jsonl-lint) and a one-line description.
6. Run npm install at the repo root so package-lock.json gains the new workspace entry, and commit the updated package-lock.json; then confirm `npm ci && npm test` passes from the repo root (CI uses npm ci, which fails if the lockfile is out of sync).
7. Sanity check by hand: `node packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js <file>` on a clean, a bad and a torn file, a missing file, and with no argument; confirm the outputs and exit codes above.
8. Open exactly one PR on suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test whose body contains the line `Closes https://github.com/suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test/issues/102`. Wait for the test workflow on the PR head to finish and make sure it is green; if it fails, fix and push to the same PR.
result.verifier:
Check out the PR head and run from the repository root. First run `npm ci`. Do one check per expect line below, in order, and report PASS or FAIL for each with the output that decided it.

Check 1 — expect: "packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js <file> prints <file>:<line>: <error> for every row that is not valid JSON (1-based lines, blank lines skipped, an unterminated last line checked) and exits 1 if any, 0 if none".
Run:
```
D=$(mktemp -d)
printf '{"a":1}\n\n{"b":2}\n' > "$D/clean.jsonl"
printf '{"a":1}\nnot json\n\n{"c":3}\n{oops}\n{"d":4}' > "$D/bad.jsonl"
printf '{"a":1}\n{"b":2}\n{"c":' > "$D/torn.jsonl"
L=packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js
node $L "$D/clean.jsonl"; echo "clean exit=$?"
node $L "$D/bad.jsonl"; echo "bad exit=$?"
node $L "$D/torn.jsonl"; echo "torn exit=$?"
```
PASS if: clean prints no error lines and exit=0; bad prints exactly two error lines, `$D/bad.jsonl:2: <non-empty error>` and `$D/bad.jsonl:5: <non-empty error>` (the path exactly as passed, then :line: and a message), and exit=1; torn prints exactly one line `$D/torn.jsonl:3: <non-empty error>` and exit=1. FAIL on any other line numbers, a missing or extra error line, a different line format, or a different exit code.

Check 2 — expect: "A missing file or no argument prints to stderr and exits 2".
Run:
```
D=$(mktemp -d); node packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js "$D/missing.jsonl" >"$D/out" 2>"$D/err"; echo "missing exit=$? stdout=$(wc -c <"$D/out") stderr=$(wc -c <"$D/err")"; node packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js >"$D/out" 2>"$D/err"; echo "noarg exit=$? stdout=$(wc -c <"$D/out") stderr=$(wc -c <"$D/err")"
```
PASS if both cases show exit=2 and stderr greater than 0 bytes. FAIL if either exit code is not 2 or stderr is empty.

Check 3 — expect: "packages/jsonl-lint/src/index.js exports lint(text) returning [{ line, error }]".
Run:
```
node --input-type=module -e "import { lint } from './packages/jsonl-lint/src/index.js'; const r = lint('{\"a\":1}\n\nnope\n{\"b\":'); console.log(JSON.stringify(r)); const ok = Array.isArray(r) && r.length===2 && r[0].line===3 && r[1].line===4 && r.every(x => Object.keys(x).sort().join()==='error,line' && typeof x.error==='string' && x.error.length>0) && lint('{\"a\":1}\n').length===0; console.log(ok ? 'LINT OK' : 'LINT BAD'); process.exit(ok?0:1)"; echo "exit=$?"
```
PASS if it prints LINT OK and exit=0. FAIL if the import fails, or it prints LINT BAD, or exit is non-zero.

Check 4 — expect: "The workspace has its own package.json (jsonl-lint, type module, test script node --test), no runtime dependencies, and node:test tests for a clean file, a bad middle row, a torn last row, blank lines and the exit codes".
Run:
```
node -e "const p=require('./packages/jsonl-lint/package.json'); console.log(p.name, p.type, p.scripts&&p.scripts.test, JSON.stringify(p.dependencies||{}))"; ls packages/jsonl-lint/test; npm test -w packages/jsonl-lint; echo "exit=$?"
```
Then read the test files under packages/jsonl-lint/.
PASS if the first line prints `jsonl-lint module node --test {}`, the workspace tests run under node:test and exit=0, and the test files contain node:test tests that exercise each of: a clean file, a bad middle row, a torn (unterminated) last row, blank lines, and the CLI exit codes. FAIL if the name, type or test script differ, any runtime dependency is declared, the tests fail, or any of those five cases has no test.

Check 5 — expect: "packages/jsonl-lint/README.md exists and the root README lists the tool".
Run:
```
test -f packages/jsonl-lint/README.md && echo readme ok; grep -n 'jsonl-lint' README.md
```
PASS if it prints `readme ok` and grep finds at least one line in the root README.md naming jsonl-lint as a tool. FAIL otherwise.

Check 6 — expect: "The change is one PR on suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test whose body says Closes https://github.com/suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test/issues/102, and npm test and the test workflow are green at its head".
Run at the repo root: `npm ci && npm test; echo "exit=$?"`. Then with the PR number N and head SHA S (GraphQL is unavailable; use REST):
```
gh api repos/suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test/pulls/N --jq '{state, head: .head.sha, body}'
gh api repos/suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test/commits/S/check-runs --jq '.check_runs[] | {name, status, conclusion}'
```
PASS if: the whole change is in that single PR on suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test; its body contains `Closes https://github.com/suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test/issues/102`; local npm test exits 0 and its output shows the jsonl-lint tests ran; and the `test` check run for the head SHA has status completed and conclusion success. FAIL if the body lacks that line, npm test fails, or the test workflow run at the head is missing, pending or not successful.

Advisory (not pass/fail): note whether package-lock.json includes the packages/jsonl-lint workspace, whether the bin has a shebang and is executable, whether CRLF line endings are handled, and whether whitespace-only lines are treated as blank.
